note: Eighths with chucks, the island strum and sixteenths as the verse, chorus and bridge of one song on G, Em, C and D at one tempo, then all three in a row over a backing track. The key is the lesson (open chords), so moves holds only a tempo range. missing: a muted stroke (a chuck) in strum-along's pattern, so the chucks on 2 and 4 are in the text only; and a strum-along pattern per section, so the whole song has no strokes drawn while the pattern changes.

exercise.title: Three strums in one song
exercise.why: The beat stays where it is under every pattern, so going from one pattern to the next only changes how fast your hand swings and which strokes touch the strings.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, strum down and up in eighths, and make the down strum on beats 2 and 4 a chuck.
Practice until the chucks land on 2 and 4 without you counting.

tool.pattern: D U D U D U D U

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. The chords and the tempo are the same, and the strum is now the island strum.
Your hand swings at the same speed as in the verse: only which strokes touch the strings is new.

tool.pattern: D . D U . U D U

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. The beat is still the same, and your hand now swings twice as fast, in sixteenths.
If your hand tightens up, strum only the downs on the beat for a bar, then let the other strokes back in.

tool.pattern: D . . U . U D U D . . U . U D U

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass on the same four chords, a bar each. Play the four bars twice with the verse strum, twice with the chorus strum and twice with the bridge strum, then start again.
If a new strum starts late, keep your hand swinging and join in on the next beat 1.
